cards.b: An increase in the proportion of a country's population living in towns and cities.
A city with a population of over 10 million.
Movement of people from the inner city to the suburbs at the edge of the urban area.
Movement of people from urban areas to rural areas, e.g. for a better quality of life.

cards.f: Where is most urban growth today?
cards.b: In Asia and Africa, in low- and middle-income countries, mainly through rural-urban migration.

cards.f: Two push factors from the countryside
cards.b: Poverty and lack of jobs; farm mechanisation; drought or conflict; poor services.

cards.f: Two pull factors to the city
cards.b: Jobs and higher wages; better schools and hospitals; family already living there.
Birth rate minus death rate; young migrants add to city growth by having children.
Congestion, transport, employment, housing, crime and environmental problems.
Housing built without permission or planning, often lacking water, sanitation and electricity.
Central business district: the commercial heart of a city, with shops, offices and banks.

cards.f: Why is the CBD the most expensive area?
cards.b: It is the most accessible point, so competition for land is highest.
The edge of a city where the built-up area meets the countryside; retail parks and new estates locate here.
The uncontrolled spread of a city into the countryside.
Often on cheap, unwanted or risky land such as steep slopes, floodplains or the city edge.

short.q: Explain two reasons why cities in low-income countries are growing rapidly.
short.model: Rural-urban migration, as people are pushed by poverty and pulled by jobs; and natural increase because migrants are young and have children.
People want a better quality of life with less pollution and congestion, and improved transport and broadband let them commute or work from home.
points: pull/enablers of rural areas or commuting

short.q: Describe two problems caused by rapid urbanisation.
short.model: Congestion because there are too many vehicles for the roads; squatter settlements because housing cannot keep up with migrants.

short.q: Explain why the CBD is located at the centre of a city.
short.model: It is the most accessible place, with road and rail links from all directions, so it has the most customers and highest land values for shops and offices.

short.q: Suggest why most megacities are now found in Asia.
short.model: Large populations, rapid industrialisation and rural-urban migration to coastal and capital cities, with high natural increase.
